card.title: 152e RÉGIMENT
card.text: Cannot be deployed unless you have 6 or more kredit slots.
card.flavorText: The 152nd Infantry Regiment is a unit of the French Army formed in 1794 during the French Revolution. It is famous notably for having fought at the Battle of Hartmannswillerkopf in the Vosges mountains during WWI, where the Germans gave it the nickname “Teufels Regiment”, meaning Devil’s Regiment. It also bears the name “First of the French Regiments” for being the first recipient of the Légion d’Honneur decoration. It has been stationed in Colmar, Alsace, since 1919 and their motto is “Do not suffer”. During WWII, the regiment was first engaged in the Battle of France with the 14th Infantry Division, led by General de Lattre de Tassigny. The division fought in the Ardennes region, especially at Rethel, where it managed to halt the German advance on the river Aisne from May 14th to June 9th. After that, it retreated orderly towards central France, and kept resisting until the Armistice was signed on June 22nd. The 152nd Regiment was then part of the Armistice Army (Vichy France), but it was disbanded in 1942 when the German forces invaded the “Zone libre”, the unoccupied part of France. Many officers and soldiers joined the Resistance in the Auvergne region at that time, where they organized numerous sabotage operations between 1942 and 1944. During the campaign for the liberation of France, they joined the First Army, and took part in the offensive on the sector of Belfort and southern Alsace. On February 8th, 1945, six days after liberating Colmar, they were back in their old quarters. They also participated in the invasion of Germany, and they were the first to enter Stuttgart on April 21st. They ended the war near Lake Constance, in Radolfzell, where they remained in charge of occupation duties until April 1946.
